key_insight: Different flow-matching paths can change SGD variance and convergence speed even when the underlying FM objective is exactly the same.
engineering_relevance: Choosing the right path is a practical optimization lever for faster and more stable training of flow-matching generative models.
method: Analyze SGD variance induced by different paths in the same FM problem class G(p_t,v*_t).
Derive a tight iteration-complexity bound for a 1D Gaussian linear velocity model and find an optimal linear path.
Formulate PathOpt_θ and convert the path constraint into sample-estimable constraints for numerical search.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds plus experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: The path constraint g_t∈G(p_t,v*_t) is not directly verifiable in practice, so approximate constraints and estimation error can affect the chosen path.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
